note: Positions 1 to 3 of the minor pentatonic scale in a key moved away from A: where position 1 sits on the whole neck, positions 1, 2 and 3 framed on one neck and played in turn, then the two crossings on two position-necks with cross. The old A-to-G text is now moves (any key, 70 to 90 bpm), so the title and text name the key and tempo as params, and the crossing tools replace the old line about tapping buttons under the neck.

exercise.title: {{=key}} minor pentatonic, positions 1 to 3
exercise.why: A position is a shape counted from its root, so in a new key all five positions slide along the neck together, and the crossings between them stay on the G string.

cells.text:
The neck below shows where position 1 of the {{=key}} minor pentatonic scale sits on the whole neck: the framed dots are the position, each one a note to play. Start on the ringed {{1}} on the low E string, play both dots on each string up to the high e string, then come back down the same way.
The goal of this practice is to find the ringed {{1}} notes without looking at the neck.

Press Play below to start the metronome at {{=bpm}}. The neck under it frames positions 1, 2 and 3 side by side. Play position 1 from its lowest note on the low E string up to the high e string and back down, one note per beat, then position 2 the same way, then position 3.
When you move to the next position, the ringed {{1}} notes sit in new places inside its frame.

The neck below shows only the crossing from position 1 to position 2: position 1 on the low strings, position 2 on the high strings. Climb position 1 from the low E string, slide on the G string from the ringed {{4}} up to the ringed {{5}}, and finish the climb in position 2.

The next neck shows the crossing from position 2 to position 3. Climb position 2, slide on the G string from the ringed {{5}} up to the ringed {{b7}}, and finish the climb in position 3. Then come back down through both crossings.
Practice until both slides land on their dot without you looking.
{{?key}}In another key the three positions sit on other frets, and both crossings are still slides on the G string.
